scan.summary: This is your own daily pre-shift inspection log for one propane forklift (unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. Each row has a date, the hour-meter reading, a tick or X for 12 check items, and the operator's initials. It is your proof that the truck was checked before use. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date, not against a written standard. The visible entries run Sep 1 to Sep 17. They show one defect (horn, Sep 9) with no record of it being fixed, and some days where the truck was used but no check was written down.
scan.freshness_note: The last visible entry is Sep 17, 2026, 10 days before today (Sep 27). The file looks like a photo of a screen: the page is tilted, a scrollbar shows on the right, and the Sep 17 row sits at the bottom edge. There may be more rows below that did not make it into the photo (inferred). Ask for a direct export or scan of the full September log. Once the month ends, also ask for the October log.

gaps.title: Horn defect with no record of taking the truck out of service or repairing it
gaps.description: On Sep 9 the horn is marked X with the note 'Horn not working'. The next day, Sep 10, it is ticked OK. Nothing in the log says whether the truck was tagged out, who repaired it, or when. As the log reads, the truck may have run a shift with a broken horn, and the fix cannot be traced.
gaps.fix: Find the repair record or work order for the FL-2 horn (Sep 9–10) and file it with this log. If the truck was used on Sep 9 after the defect was found, write down what happened. Add a 'defect reported to / corrective action / date returned to service / initials' column or section to the log form, so every X has a written close-out.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) (examine before each shift; report and correct defects) and 1910.178(p)(1) (a truck needing repair is taken out of service until restored). Oregon OSHA adopts 1910.178 by reference in Division 2, Subdivision N (OAR 437-002-0220) and has its own additions in OAR 437-002-0227, 'Additional Oregon Rules for Powered Industrial Trucks'. I confirmed that rule exists, but not that it adds anything about inspection records.
gaps.locator: page 1, Sep 9 row (Horn column and Notes) and Sep 10 row

gaps.title: No visible entries after Sep 17
gaps.description: The visible log stops at Sep 17, and today is Sep 27. Either about seven working days of checks were not recorded, or the photo cut off the rest of the table. The screen-photo framing makes the second more likely, but the document cannot show which (inferred).
gaps.fix: Get the full September log as an export or a flat scan of every row. If there are truly no entries after Sep 17, check whether FL-2 was used (hour meter, dispatch records) and restart daily entries now.
gaps.locator: page 1, bottom of the table (last visible row Sep 17)

gaps.title: No entries for Sep 3 and Sep 4, but the hour meter shows the truck was used
gaps.description: The log jumps from Sep 2 (4,819 hours) to Sep 7 (4,834 hours), a 15-hour gap. On other days the meter goes up about 6–7 hours per shift. So the truck ran for roughly one to two more shifts between Sep 2 and Sep 7 with no check recorded (inferred from the hour readings). By my count Sep 3–4, 2026 fall on Thursday and Friday (inferred).
gaps.fix: Ask the operators and supervisor whether FL-2 ran on Sep 3 and/or Sep 4 and whether it was checked. Record what you find with a dated note. Do not back-fill ticks after the fact. Remind operators that every shift the truck is used needs its own entry.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The federal rule requires the check before each shift but does not require it to be written down. The log is your evidence, so gaps weaken it.
gaps.locator: page 1, between the Sep 2 and Sep 7 rows (Hours column)

gaps.title: Operators listed by initials only, with no signature or supervisor review
gaps.description: Each entry names the operator only by initials ('M.C.', 'J.R.'). There is no full name, signature, or supervisor sign-off anywhere on the page, so it is hard to tie an entry to a trained, evaluated operator.
gaps.fix: Add a key at the top or bottom of the form that matches initials to full names. Add a line for a supervisor to review and sign weekly or monthly. Check that M.C. and J.R. are on your operator training and evaluation records.
gaps.locator: page 1, Operator column. No signature or review block in the document.

I am less sure the capture is complete. It looks like a photo of a screen, with a scrollbar and the bottom row at the edge of the image, so entries after Sep 17 may exist but were not captured.
